title: Schooling and synchronised emergence vs a predator: per-capita escape (agent-based model)
evidence_kind: simulated: model output under declared assumptions; not an observation of any fish, predator or lineage

model.name: claude-eco collective/1: 2-D agent-based school (zonal model geometry, detection, alarm cascade over the neighbour graph), predator approach/burst/strike with confusion, gliders flying the project point-mass glide distance
model.context: Population/behavioural layer of the collective scale; the rigid-body/hydrodynamic collective launch is claude-organ's. Compares glide + alarm, glide independent, swim + alarm and swim-only over N = 1..64. All behavioural parameters are assumptions, swept. SIMULATION, not an observation of any school.

findings: Solitary (N=1) capture per attack: glide 0.69, swim 0.99.
N=16: P(capture per episode) glide+alarm 0.133 +- 0.027 (95%), glide independent 0.773, swim+alarm 0.953, swim 0.882.
Per-capita capture per encounter at N=16: glide+alarm 0.0083 vs solitary glider 0.692 (83x lower); glide independent 0.0483; swim 0.0551 (dilution alone).

In this model, the alarm cascade helps any prey whose escape takes it out of the predator's reach: it lowers whole-school capture for gliders (launch at 10-18 m/s) but not for swimmers at the default 1.7 m/s flee speed. It is a speed-of-escape effect; gliding is one way to get that speed (see the U_flee = 10 m/s row).

Sensitivity (15 one-at-a-time settings, N = 1, 8, 32, B = 300): glide + alarm has lower whole-school capture than glide-independent at N = 32 in 15 of 15; per-capita capture of a glider in a school of 32 is below a solitary glider's in 15 of 15. With no confusion effect (kappa = 0) glide + alarm still drops from 0.68 (N = 1) to 0.50 (N = 32) while glide-independent rises to 0.92. If swimmers could flee at 10 m/s (= the launch exit speed), the alarm helps them too: swim + alarm 0.59 -> 0.03.

Per unit time, if encounters scale with school size (alpha = 1, no dilution), risk relative to a solitary fish at N = 32 is: glide_sync 0.26, glide_indep 1.16, swim_sync 0.98, swim 0.83 (alpha = 0 and 0.5 in results.json).
Episodes per estimate (B): main:1,2,4,8,16,32 B=600; main:64 B=300; sensitivity B=300. The N=64 shard at B=600 was stopped by the 1800 s process cap (exit 143, no result) and rerun at B=300.

does_not_establish: that real flying-fish schools emerge synchronously or transmit alarms
that gliding is uniquely required for the alarm benefit: swimmers fleeing at 10 m/s get it too in this model
costs of the alarm cascade (false alarms, energy of needless launches)
rigid-body or hydrodynamic interactions between launching fish (claude-organ's layer)
encounter-rate scaling with school size (alpha is swept, not estimated)
confusion strengths for any real predator (Landeau & Terborgh form only)
any 3-D effect: the ABM is 2-D top view; airborne fish are represented by their ground track
